description: Qorix project-lifecycle context — capture ideas and walk them idea→backlog→pi→released as a flat, self-hosted store, link a pi item into the needs graph, cut releases with deterministic version bumps, driven by `qik nexus`.

priming.description: Recall the pipeline state from the store, not from memory.

steps.label: Capture
steps.description: Record a new entry at any stage (idea/backlog/pi). The why is mandatory — an idea without a purpose can never become an intent. Declare --change breaking/feature/fix on anything that will ship, for version derivation.

steps.label: Link into the graph
steps.prompt: When a pi item is taken on, author the needs it gives rise to in the sphinx-needs source first, then record the coupling with `qik nexus link <ID> <NEED>...`. Link only ids that already exist in the graph, so `qik axon check` stays clean.
steps.description: The one edge from the lifecycle store up into the traceability graph. nexus validates id format but never authors or reads the needs themselves. Use `qik nexus unlink <ID> <NEED>...` to remove stale need-ids after renames.

steps.label: Author needs with qik-thalam / review with pharaoh
steps.prompt: When authoring new needs nodes (sys_req, sys_arc, prd_glob_req, etc.) always use the @qik-thalam subagent — it is the sole persona authorized to write directly into needs/. For requirements review and quality checks invoke pharaoh (pharaoh.req-review, pharaoh.arch-review, etc.). Concept-level needs — especially sys_req__concept__*_enabler and sys_arc__concept__*_enabler — must cite the specific ISO norm clause they realize: ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288 §6.4.x for structural positioning, plus the enabler's own content norm with specific clause anchors (ISO 26262 §x for saf_, ISO/SAE 21434 clause x for sec_, ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-3 §x for tst_, ISO/IEC/IEEE 26511/26514 §x for doc_). Name both the norm and the clause — never just the norm. prd_ is grounded directly in 15288 and has no second content norm.
steps.description: Authoring gate: qik-thalam writes needs/, pharaoh reviews them. Concept enabler needs must reference 15288 structural positioning AND the enabler-specific content norm with clause precision.

steps.label: Attach external reference
steps.description: Attach a structured external-tracker reference (e.g. a GitHub issue URL or Jira key) to any entry. Each ref gets an auto-assigned id (ref-001, ref-002, ...). Remove a stale ref with `qik nexus unref <ID> <REF_ID_OR_WHAT:LOCATOR>`.

steps.label: Tracker sync
steps.description: Connect to configured trackers and pull/reconcile. `nexus connect` lists all configured trackers (url/project/user/token status) from .qik/nexus/config.toml. `nexus pull` imports new open assigned issues as idea entries and reconciles existing non-terminal refs (headline drift, closed→advance). Never touches staged/released entries. `nexus push` posts a progress comment on-demand. `nexus track <cr> <tracker> <locator>` links a CR to an issue; `nexus untrack <cr> <tracker>` removes the link. `nexus ping <tracker>` tests auth. Write a tracker block: `nexus connect <name> --type github|jira --url <url> --project <project> [--user <user>]`.

steps.label: Release + version
steps.description: Preview each target's current and derived-next version read-only before `qik nexus bump <target>` rewrites it and `qik nexus release` closes the increment. The next number is computed from the current one and the released items' change natures, never guessed.

output.note: `qik nexus ... --mcp` emits the same JSON shape the qik-mcp server exposes via the nexus_* tools.
